result.explanation: The $150 charge at WGC Dunkin is coded as POI funding transactions, which is a funds load or transfer. Policy §V.B.1.b prohibits cash and cash-like transactions. The card's history shows no recognition program or similar exception. It mostly buys lab chemicals and equipment, plus some catering. This is the card's only charge at this merchant. Other agencies using the merchant doesn't clear it.
result.policy_clause: §V.B.1.b — Cash, including cash advances and ATM transactions
result.innocent_explanation: A Dunkin prepaid card or app reload bought for an approved employee recognition purpose or a work event. A receipt or approval would be needed to show that.

result.explanation: Single QIAGEN lab-reagent purchase (RNeasy kit, buffer) of $1,367.10 on a lab card whose history is mostly lab/medical supplies (LifeTech, Agilent, Parse). The card has 3 QIAGEN charges. No same-day or adjacent QIAGEN charges, so no split or double charge. Amount is within QIAGEN's typical range (median $567, 90th percentile $1,910) and normal for the agency. Not prohibited or personal.
result.innocent_explanation: Routine lab reagent purchase from a regular life-science supplier for research use at the health sciences center.

result.explanation: $10 QuikTrip gift card funding (MCC "POI funding") falls under the prohibited gift-card/cash clause, unless it was for employee recognition. The card's history shows no recognition label. It does show 19 Tango Card reward-type purchases, and the agency made 114 similar QuikTrip purchases. I could not confirm the purpose from the data. Need the recognition program approval or the receipt/recipient log.
result.policy_clause: §V.B.1.d — Gift Certificates (except purchases for employee recognition); §V.B.1.b — Cash
result.innocent_explanation: The card appears to run a reward program (19 Tango Card purchases), so this $10 gift card may be an employee recognition award, which the policy allows.

result.explanation: Single $1,883 charge for molecular biology reagents (Phusion polymerase, Gibson Assembly mix) at a lab-supply vendor. This card buys from New England Biolabs regularly (28 purchases, e.g. $731 on 2024-08-21) alongside DNA oligos and research chemicals. No same-day or nearby NEB charge, so no split or duplicate. Fits the card's research profile. No prohibited or personal indicators.
result.innocent_explanation: Routine lab reagent order for research; NEB is among this card's top merchants and the agency's heaviest vendor use.

result.explanation: Motor fuel is on the policy's prohibited list (§V.B.1.e), and fuel for state vehicles belongs on the ComData card. This card's history shows mostly Amazon, Walmart, Hobby Lobby and uniforms. The only fuel purchase in the window is this one (T202503038593), and I saw no recognition program or non-state-vehicle exception. Other agencies buying fuel at this merchant does not clear it. The amount is small.
result.policy_clause: §V.B.1.e — Motor Fuel or Fluids; FAQ: the ComData card must be used for fuel for state-owned vehicles
result.innocent_explanation: Fuel for a non-state vehicle, such as a rental or event vehicle, or a one-off emergency fill-up. Nothing in the card history shows this.

result.explanation: gBlocks gene fragments from a DNA synthesis vendor fit this lab card, which buys molecular biology supplies (NEB, VWR, Illumina). The card has five IDT charges, and the same gBlocks item recurs on 2024-08-09 ($403.50) and 2024-08-25 ($203.50) at different amounts. The $503.50 charge has no same-day or next-day sibling and no matching duplicate, so there is no split or double charge. IDT is also a routine merchant for this agency.
result.innocent_explanation: Routine research purchase of custom gene fragments for a lab, consistent with the card's repeat IDT orders.

result.explanation: A single $500 charge for digital flyer distribution at Peachjar, a school flyer service used by 3 agencies, including this one ($1,320 across 2 purchases). It's within Peachjar's normal range (median $742). The card history shows comparable outreach and education purchases (Canva, Kahoot, name badges). No split, repeat charge, or prohibited or personal category was found nearby.
result.innocent_explanation: Routine outreach flyer distribution to schools by a health sciences center program, consistent with its Canva, Kahoot and badge purchases.

result.explanation: A single $611.12 charge at TEMP CONTROL SYSTEMS, electrical parts. The merchant is this card's top vendor (25 of 53 transactions), and the card buys only electrical parts. The amount is within the card's range (median $159.90, largest $1,187.62). No same-day or nearby charges at this merchant around 7/25, so there is no split or double charge.
